{{Short description|Japanese samurai and Shinto priest (1815–1890)}}
'''Hirayama Seisai''' (1815–1890) was a Japanese samurai and Shinto priest during the late Edo period and early Meiji era. He was born in Mitsu, Fukushima, and at the age of 20, traveled to Edo (now Tokyo) to study [[Chinese literature]], [[Japanese literature]], and other subjects. In 1850, he became the adopted son of a government official and inherited his position. During the late [[Edo period]], he served as a close advisor to the [[Tokugawa shogunate]] as a senior vassal.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=神道大成教 - SHINDEN |url=http://shinden.boo.jp/wiki/%E7%A5%9E%E9%81%93%E5%A4%A7%E6%88%90%E6%95%99 |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=shinden.boo.jp}}</ref> After the [[Meiji Restoration]], he briefly retired from public life, but later became a Shinto priest and held various positions at shrines in [[Tokyo]] and [[Miyagi Prefecture|Miyagi]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=神道大成教 - Enpedia |url=https://enpedia.rxy.jp/wiki/%E7%A5%9E%E9%81%93%E5%A4%A7%E6%88%90%E6%95%99 |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=enpedia.rxy.jp}}{{User-generated source|date=January 2024}}</ref>{{User-generated source|date=January 2024}} In 1872, he founded the [[Shinto Taiseikyo|Shinto Taisei]] sect and served as its first head,<ref name=":0" /> he rallied for independence as a [[Sect Shinto|Shinto Sect]] in 1879, and gained it in 1882.<ref name=":1">井上順孝『教派神道の形成』（弘文堂　1991年） 朝日日本歴史人物事典（朝日新聞出版）<!-- uncertain origin from Japanese Wikipedia article https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%B9%B3%E5%B1%B1%E7%9C%81%E6%96%8E --></ref><ref>Sugada 1994, p.178-180 Masaaki Sugata "Old Shindo Revives" Tachibana Publishing, 1994 菅田正昭『古神道は甦る』橘出版、1994年</ref><ref name=":3" />{{User-generated source|date=January 2024}}<ref>{{Cite web |title=神道大成教（しんとうたいせいきょう）の意味 - goo国語辞書 |url=https://dictionary.goo.ne.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E9%81%93%E5%A4%A7%E6%88%90%E6%95%99/ |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=goo辞書 |language=ja}}</ref> During his tenure as president [[Mitake-kyo]] also gained independence<ref name=":1" /> He died on May 22, 1890. His writings include "The Truth of Our Sect" and "The True Method of Cultivating the Way."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=小項目事典 |first=朝日日本歴史人物事典,デジタル版 日本人名大辞典+Plus,ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 |title=平山省斎(ひらやま・せいさい)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%B9%B3%E5%B1%B1%E7%9C%81%E6%96%8E-121637 |access-date=2023-01-24 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref>
